failure_modes: Intranasal delivery failure: intact EVs do not reach olfactory-bulb–adjacent tissue, CSF, or microglia in amounts sufficient to cause or be detected as a reproducible transcriptional change (matches ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Assay sensitivity floor: orthogonal detection (particle counts co-localized with capture signal and spike-in recovery) lacks the sensitivity/ specificity in short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue samples, yielding false negatives and making correlation with single-cell readouts unmeasurable (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Spike-in nonrepresentativeness: the exogenous spike-in tracer behaves differently in vivo from endogenous therapeutic EVs (different biodistribution, retention, clearance, or capture-epitope exposure), so recovery metrics do not reflect true intact-EV exposure and mislead interpretation (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Species/route generalizability: positive rodent functional reports after intranasal EV dosing (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi) are not predictive of intact-EV biodistribution in other species or under the exact formulation/administration conditions used here, causing contradictory expectations and failed verification in the proposed assay (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).

Secretome confounding: soluble cargo or non-vesicular particles that survive fractionation or membrane disruption mediate microglial transcriptional changes, so detergent/protease or capture-depletion arms do not abolish the signature and the experiment cannot attribute effect to intact EVs (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; supported by absence of orthogonal exposure linkage in many rodent studies ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Operational timing mismatch: the predefined short post-dose interval may miss the true window of intact-EV tissue presence or microglial transcriptional response (either too early for transcriptional change or too late after transient exposure), producing inconsistent or null single-cell signatures despite exposure being possible (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Capture-reagent interference: immuno-capture reagents or buffers required for orthogonal verification alter EV integrity or microglial responsiveness (during spike-in recovery or in vitro controls), invalidating exposure/readout concordance (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
strongest_objection: The proposal can fail because intranasal administration simply does not deliver a biologically meaningful amount of intact, membrane-protected EVs to the sampled CNS compartments at the chosen short post-dose interval (or the delivered intact-EV fraction is below orthogonal assay sensitivity), so there will be no reproducible linkage between verified in vivo intact-EV exposure and any ex vivo microglial single-cell transcriptional signature. This is supported by direct non-human-primate biodistribution data showing negligible brain/CSF recovery and strong nasal retention after intranasal EV dosing (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution); even if rodent efficacy papers report functional outcomes after intranasal EVs (ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi), those do not establish orthogonally verified intact-EV exposure and may reflect formulation-, species-, or secretome-dependent effects. Compounding this, MISEV2023 warns that EV separation/characterization and membrane-protection assays are technically challenging and that spike-in or capture reagents may not faithfully report in vivo EV behavior (ev-misev2023-quality-framework). Together, these imply a bounded failure mode where either (a) real intact-EV exposure is absent in vivo, or (b) intact-EV exposure is present but below detection/verification limits or not faithfully reported by the spike-in/capture assays, producing no reliable correlation with the single-cell readout.
